model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; normalised earnings after capital retention, net debt zero; residual-income on tangible book cross-check)

equity_bridge.item: Excess CET1 capital above a ~12% operating target (haircut for possible AOCI recognition)
equity_bridge.note: Q3 2026 10-Q: CET1 capital $71,745m on RWA $520,429m = 13.8%; requirement incl. 4.5% stress capital buffer is 9.0% through 1 Jan 2028. Surplus over a 12% operating target is $9.3bn on the filed basis. But COF excludes AOCI from regulatory capital as a Category III bank, and the Basel III finalisation proposal would recognise AFS marks (~$10.4bn gross unrealised loss): on that basis CET1 is ~12.3% and the surplus ~$1.5bn. $6.0bn is held from the September build as roughly the midpoint; the $11bn/yr buyback pace and the $1bn preferred redemption show management treats the capital as surplus.
Non-cumulative perpetual preferred, 30 Sep 2026 10-Q Table A; 3,980,700 shares after the $1.0bn Series M redemption on 1 Sep 2026. Senior to common; flows are pre-preferred-dividend.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-path average. Every statutory CAGR is distorted by the May 2025 all-stock Discover acquisition (revenue and equity step-ups, FY2025 EPS 4.03 depressed by the Q2 2025 Day-1 CECL loss). Pre-deal organic revenue grew 8.7%/yr FY21-24 in a period of card-balance rebuilding and rising rates; forward balance-sheet growth of 4-5% is more representative.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (29.3% 3yr) diverges >30% from revenue (16.0%) and EPS (-39.2%): all three are acquisition artefacts, not organic trends. Free-cash-flow CAGRs are not meaningful for a bank (OCF includes provision add-backs and loan-sale flows) and are left null.
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted FCF CAGR is not computed: owner-FCF is not the model for a bank. SBC grew $513m (FY23) -> $776m (FY25) largely from Discover replacement awards, roughly in line with revenue.
historical_growth.tbv_per_share_fy24_to_q3_26: $106.97 (FY24) -> $107.72 (FY25) -> $102.72 (Q3 26), company definition: flat-to-down through the Discover deal and the 2026 rise in rates (AOCI)

scenario_narratives.base: The Discover integration completes on schedule (back-book converted during 2027, $2.5bn run-rate synergies, currently tracking ahead) and the efficiency gain already visible in 9M26 is half kept. Credit normalises to through-cycle levels rather than staying at the 2026 reserve-release run-rate: the base earns ~$12.5bn normalised against ~$14-16bn annualised adjusted earnings today. Normalised ROTE ~22% on required tangible equity, 3-5% balance-sheet growth, ~75-85% of earnings returned. Value lands at ~2.2x tangible book against ~1.8x at the market: the market is discounting through-cycle credit worse than this base or a cost of equity nearer 13%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Owning the Discover/PULSE rails proves to be the Amex-style structural advantage the deal was sold on: COF's own volume migrates, network and interchange economics stay in-house, Brex compounds commercial card, and credit stays benign. Efficiency falls to ~49% and ROTE settles in the low-to-mid 20s.
scenario_narratives.bear: A US recession arrives after a rate-hiking phase while two integrations are live. Card NCOs rise to ~7% on a book with roughly double its nearest competitor's subprime share, CECL front-loads the reserve build (FY27 earnings fall ~55%), synergies slip, and the inherited Discover misclassification matter and subprime-concentration scrutiny cost more than accrued. Through-cycle ROTE resets to the mid-teens. The excess capital cushions the downturn without a raise.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Capital One is valued as a bank: normalised free cash flow to equity (earnings after the capital needed to grow the balance sheet) capitalised at an 11.3% cost of equity, with deposits and debt treated as operating funding (net debt zero), preferred deducted, and a haircut CET1 surplus credited. The base year is a normalised FY2026E that strips integration costs, acquired-intangible amortisation and the 2026 reserve releases, and charges a through-cycle provision well above what the company is currently booking. A residual-income check on ~$102 of tangible book per share is recorded in inputs.notes. Against the September build the value fell ~8%, almost entirely because the 10-year Treasury rose from ~4.2% to ~5.1%; the business itself came in better (fewer shares, better efficiency, improving credit).
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: every 1pp of revenue in provisions is ~$500m of after-tax earnings (~$0.85/share per year); the base assumes through-cycle, not current, charge-offs.
Cost of equity: the 0.8pp rise in the risk-free rate since September cost ~$24/share; each 1pp is worth roughly 12-14%.
Excess capital ($6bn, ~$10/share) depends on AOCI staying out of regulatory capital; on an AOCI-inclusive basis the surplus is ~$1.5bn.
AOCI of -$10.0bn depresses tangible book and accretes back as securities pull to par -- unmodelled upside, and the mirror of the risk above.
Synergy realisation and back-book network migration through 2027; management gives no efficiency-ratio guidance.
Inherited Discover card-misclassification inquiry (SEC; ~$1.2bn restitution largely accrued) and the NY AG antitrust probe are charged only in the bear case.
valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_banner: Sanity check tripped on P/E only (2026-11-19), the same trip as the September build: the weighted value implies 83.5x FY2025 SBC-adjusted EPS (~$2.60) against a 10-year average of 20.3x. That is a denominator artefact, not an over-rich model. FY2025 GAAP net income ($2,453m, EPS $4.03) contains the Q2 2025 loss of -$4,277m (Day-1 CECL reserve build on acquired Discover loans plus merger costs) and only ~7.5 months of Discover earnings on a share count that already carries the ~256m shares issued for the deal. The model never uses FY2025 as its base: it capitalises a normalised FY2026E FCFE that is itself below current reported earnings, so the priority-1 remedy (normalise the earnings base) is already built in and no driver was changed. Against honest denominators the same value is ~13.8x trailing-twelve-month SBC-adjusted EPS to Q3 2026 (~$15.7; the market price is ~11.7x) and ~10.7x normalised FY2026E EPS to common (~$20.3), both below the 20.3x average and far inside the 40.6x trip line. The other rules pass: P/B 1.23x (10-year max 1.33x) and P/Sales 2.62x (max 2.84x) sit near the top of their ranges because the all-stock Discover purchase added ~$47bn of goodwill and intangibles to book and lifted the margin structure; on tangible book the value is ~2.1x against ~1.8x at market. The other fixes on the list were rejected: clearing the P/E rule on FY2025 EPS needs a value below ~$106, about tangible book for a ~20% ROTE bank; a regulatory WACC premium would double-count risk already in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, on top of a cost of equity that has just risen 0.8pp with the risk-free rate; the growth path (3-5%) is already below the through-cycle revenue CAGR; EV/EBITDA exit caps do not apply to a bank. The trip will clear by itself when FY2026 becomes the latest annual row. Framing: a ~20% ROTE card franchise returning 75-85% of earnings, bought for income plus modest compounding; the risk is the credit cycle.

data_sources.financials: COF_Metrics.csv and KPIs (through Q3 2026) plus the Q3 2026 10-Q text (COF_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt): cover share count, Table A TCE reconciliation, CET1 capital and RWA, preferred, AOCI, integration expense, intangible amortisation, cash flow statement.

bridge.item: Anchor refresh to Q3 2026 10-Q: diluted shares 616.5m -> 604.5m, preferred 5,407 -> 4,419, FY26E revenue base 63,500 -> 64,000
Anchor refresh: risk-free 4.2% -> 5.07% moves cost of equity 10.5% -> 11.3%
Methodology: capital retention struck on filed CET1 (0.976 x g) instead of estimated required TCE (0.855 x g)
Driver change: base efficiency 51.0/50.6% -> 50.5/50.2% on 9M26 evidence (base margin +0.5/+0.4pp)

bridge.note: no effect on intrinsic value; upside and band only
ties to probability_weighted.weighted_iv; each step is a full engine rebuild

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E total net revenue (net interest income + non-interest income). 9M26 actual 47,425 (Q1 15,231, Q2 15,850, Q3 16,344; Q3 2026 10-Q) plus Q4 at ~16,575 (Q3 run-rate +1.4% on seasonal purchase volume; NIM 8.41% in Q3). FY2025 statutory 53,434 contains only 7.5 months of Discover and is not a usable base. FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027.
inputs.share_count_basis: 601.5m common shares outstanding at 30 Sep 2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q cover: 601,533,153) plus ~3m dilutive RSU/PSU (Q3 weighted diluted 609.5m is an average struck before the quarter's $2.7bn of buybacks). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and buybacks (9M26 $8,224m) are the distribution channel for the FCFE and the excess capital credited in the equity bridge -- reducing the count as well would double-count.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is ZERO by construction. Capital One is a bank holding company: deposits ($480.7bn at 30 Sep 2026) and senior/sub debt and securitisations ($47.7bn) are operating funding whose cost is inside net interest income; cash ($48.9bn) is liquidity held against that funding, not surplus. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt and cash recorded for audit only.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E normalised FCFE (pre-preferred) = normalised NPAT ~12,540 (64,000 x pre-tax 24.8% x (1 - 21%)) less capital retained ~2,810 to grow required CET1 with a 4.5% balance sheet (0.976 x g x revenue). Pre-tax 24.8% = 100 - adjusted efficiency 50.5% - through-cycle provision 24.7%. This is deliberately BELOW what the company is printing: 9M26 GAAP NI 8,733 plus after-tax integration expense (~$1.15bn pre-tax) and acquired-intangible amortisation ($1,507m pre-tax) is ~10.8bn for nine months (~14.4bn annualised), because the 9M26 provision ran at 21.0% of revenue (NCOs 22.4%, with reserve releases of $662m in Q2 and $225m in Q3) against the 24.7% normalised here.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory OCF less capex (FY2025 26,140; 1H26 13,547) is inflated by the non-cash provision add-back and loan-sale/trading movements and is meaningless as free cash flow for a bank. reported_fcf here is the normalised FCFE proxy BEFORE the SBC charge, so last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation (cash flow statement add-back): FY2024 $569m, FY2025 $776m (includes Discover replacement awards), 1H26 $346m -> ~$700m FY2026E run-rate, ~1.1% of revenue. Net-share-settlement withholding taxes are not separately material in the XBRL facts.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income IS the banking business, and no cash is added in the bridge (matching-asset rule satisfied the other way).
inputs.buyback_note: 9M26 repurchases $8,224m (Q1 2,793, Q2 2,747, Q3 2,684) under the $16bn authorisation, after FY2025 $4,099m. The ~$11bn annualised pace exceeds normalised FCFE (~$9.7bn): COF is running down the post-Discover CET1 surplus (14.4% at Q1 -> 13.8% at Q3), consistent with the excess-capital line in the equity bridge. Series M preferred ($1.0bn) was also redeemed on 1 Sep 2026.
inputs.book_value_anchor: 30 Sep 2026 (Q3 10-Q Table A): stockholders' equity $109,656m - preferred $4,419m - goodwill and intangibles net of related deferred tax $43,446m = tangible common equity $61,791m = $102.72/share on 601.5m outstanding ($102.2 on the 604.5m diluted count). The September build used gross intangibles without the deferred-tax offset (~$98 at Q2 vs the company's $105.21); the company's definition is used from here. TBV/share FELL in Q3 ($105.21 -> $102.72) despite $3.4bn of earnings to common because AOCI widened to -$10,008m (from -$5,468m at Dec 2025) as rates rose: AFS securities carry $10.4bn of gross unrealised losses. That pulls to par over the securities' lives (unmodelled upside of up to ~$16/share pre-tax-effect) but would cut CET1 if the Basel III finalisation proposal makes Category III banks recognise AFS marks.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: US 10-year Treasury 5.07% (CBOE ^TNX, 18 Nov 2026; it was ~4.2% at the September build) + beta 1.25 x US ERP 5.0% = 11.3%. The same spot-risk-free construction as September, refreshed: rates have risen materially (the Q3 10-Q's market-implied Fed funds upper bound is 4.25% for Dec 2026 and 5.00% for Dec 2027, against 3.25% assumed in the FY2025 10-K). Beta 1.25 reflects a subprime-skewed card lender. One rate across all three scenarios; credit-cycle, integration and regulatory risk is charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial (operating lease ROU assets ~$1.5bn vs $114bn equity); lease cost sits inside non-interest expense and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interests. Preferred stock is a senior claim: deducted at its $4,419m carrying value (3,980,700 shares after the Series M redemption) in the equity bridge, and the flows are pre-preferred.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine (same model as the 2026-09-26 build and as NAB.AX). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with capital retention = g x required regulatory capital is the clean-surplus equivalent and runs through the validated engine, which also produces the workbook. An owner-FCF DCF is not usable: deposits are operating funding, not net debt, and statutory OCF less capex (9M26 ~$19bn) is inflated by the provision add-back. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = total net revenue; ebitda_margin_path = normalised pre-tax profit (revenue - non-interest expense ex integration costs and ex acquired-intangible amortisation - through-cycle provision) PLUS SBC, as % of revenue; sbc_pct_path 1.1%; da_pct 0; capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED = 0.976 x g (12% CET1 x RWA $520.4bn / revenue $64.0bn); cash_tax_rate_path 21% (9M26 effective 21.2%); wacc = cost of equity 11.3%; net_debt = 0. Equity bridge: + excess CET1, - preferred. UPDATE 2026-11-19 (prior build 2026-09-26, on the Q2 2026 balance sheet). ANCHORS REFRESHED to the Q3 2026 10-Q: shares 616.5m -> 604.5m; preferred 5,407 -> 4,419; FY26E revenue 63,500 -> 64,000; risk-free 4.2% -> 5.07%, so cost of equity 10.5% -> 11.3%. DRIVERS CHANGED: (1) base margin +0.5pp FY27 / +0.4pp FY28+ (efficiency 51.0/50.6 -> 50.5/50.2): 9M26 adjusted efficiency was 49.9% (Q3 48.7%) against the 51.5% assumed for FY26E, with synergies running ahead of schedule; half of the beat is passed through because Q4 is seasonally heavy on marketing and part of the gain is a rate-driven NIM (8.41%) that may not persist. (2) capital retention is now struck on filed regulatory capital (12% x RWA = $62.4bn, 0.976 x g) rather than the estimated required TCE (0.855 x g) -- CET1 and RWA were not available in September. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: growth paths (rates are a tailwind to yield but already in the FY26E base; would move on FY27 loan growth outside 3-6%); through-cycle provision 25.7%/25.5% of revenue (9M26 ran 21.0% and Q3 total NCO rate 2.73%, domestic card 3.98%, but Q3 is the seasonal low and two quarters of releases are not a cycle; would move after four quarters of total NCOs under 3.0% with flat delinquencies -- 30+ day delinquency actually rose to 3.41% in Q3); bull and bear margin paths; SBC 1.1%; tax 21%; terminal growth; weights 25/50/25; excess-capital credit $6.0bn (now based on filed numbers, see bridge note); exclusion of integration costs and intangible amortisation. RESIDUAL-INCOME CROSS-CHECK: normalised FY26E NPAT 12,540 on required tangible equity ~$55.8bn (TCE 61.8 less 6.0 excess) = ROTE ~22.5% (reported Q3 ROTE 21.1%, 9M 17.0%); steady-state P/TBV = (22.5 - 3)/(11.3 - 3) = 2.35x x 55.8 = $131bn, + 6.0 - 4.4 = $132.7bn = ~$220/share, against the engine base of ~$224. LEGAL: the 360 Savings matter is settled ($425m class settlement approved April 2026, provided for) and no longer sits in the bear case. The inherited Discover card-misclassification matter (SEC inquiry; ~$1.2bn merchant restitution, largely accrued by Discover before close) and the NY AG antitrust probe are not charged in base; the bear margin carries them. DATA NOTE: COF_Analysis.json quotes a Q3 2026 domestic card charge-off rate of 4.63% -- that is the Q3 2025 comparative; the Q3 2026 10-Q shows 3.98%.

bear.growth_rationale: US recession in FY27 after a rate-hiking phase: card balances shrink in real terms, fee income falls with purchase volume; network migration friction costs premium/travel accounts. Terminal 2.0%. UNCHANGED.
bear.margin_rationale: FY27 10.6% = 100 - efficiency 52.5% (synergies delayed, integration costs charged) - provision 38.0% (card NCOs ~7%, CECL reserve build) + 1.1%; comparable to FY2020. FY28 17.1% as reserves peak. Mature 22.1% = 100 - 52.0 - 27.0 + 1.1: through-cycle credit permanently worse on the enlarged subprime book, part of the synergy competed or regulated away (interchange/APR caps, the Discover misclassification remediation, NY AG subprime-concentration scrutiny). Numbers UNCHANGED; the settled 360 Savings case is no longer the driver.
bear.capex_rationale: Capital retained to grow regulatory capital with the balance sheet = 0.976 x g (12% CET1 x RWA $520.4bn / FY26E revenue $64.0bn). At 5% growth 4.9% of revenue (~$3.3bn, ~25% of NPAT); at 3% terminal 2.9%. Low retention in FY27-28 because the balance sheet barely grows; the excess capital in the bridge absorbs the recession.

base.growth_rationale: Total net revenue. UNCHANGED from September. FY27 5.0%: a full year of Brex, Discover network revenue as the credit back-book migrates through 2027, and ~4% card-loan growth. Tapers to 3.0%.
base.margin_rationale: Normalised pre-tax profit + SBC on revenue. FY27 24.9% = 100 - efficiency 50.5% - provision 25.7% + SBC 1.1%; FY28+ 25.4% = 100 - 50.2 - 25.5 + 1.1. Efficiency improved 0.5/0.4pp on 9M26 evidence (adjusted 49.9%, Q3 48.7%, vs 51.5% assumed for FY26E); provision left at through-cycle although 9M26 ran 21.0%. Pre-deal FY2019 ran ~25.6% on the same basis.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to grow regulatory capital with the balance sheet = 0.976 x g (12% CET1 x RWA $520.4bn / FY26E revenue $64.0bn). At 5% growth 4.9% of revenue (~$3.3bn, ~25% of NPAT); at 3% terminal 2.9%.

bull.growth_rationale: Discover network takes a growing share of COF's own card and debit volume plus third-party issuers; Brex compounds in commercial card; card-loan growth ~5-6%. Terminal 3.5%.
bull.margin_rationale: Full $2.7bn synergy upside retained plus network economics beyond the deal model: efficiency 50.3% -> 49.0%, provision 25.2% -> 24.8% (benign unemployment, NCOs near 4.5% card), + SBC 1.1%. UNCHANGED: Q3 adjusted efficiency of 48.7% shows the path is reachable but does not move it.
bull.capex_rationale: Capital retained to grow regulatory capital with the balance sheet = 0.976 x g (12% CET1 x RWA $520.4bn / FY26E revenue $64.0bn). At 5% growth 4.9% of revenue (~$3.3bn, ~25% of NPAT); at 3% terminal 2.9%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 25/50/25 (house default 15/50/35). Bear stays at 25%: ~75% of revenue is unsecured consumer card lending skewed to subprime/near-prime; 2026 earnings benefit from reserve releases; 30+ day delinquency ticked up to 3.41% in Q3 while rates are rising; two integrations run concurrently and management still declines to guide an efficiency ratio; the Discover misclassification inquiry and NY AG probe are open. The 360 Savings settlement removed one tail, which is offset by the rate backdrop. Bull held at 25%: it requires network economics beyond the guided synergies and benign credit for a decade. Would move toward 20/50/30 on a second year of total NCOs near 3% with the back-book conversion complete.
probability_weighted.band_note: band_position is negative because the price sits BELOW both the house (SBC-expensed) and street (SBC-as-non-cash) weighted values; it is not located between them.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

diagnosis.detail: Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: regulatory single point of failure

sanity_check.fix_applied: 2026-11-19, one pass: NO DRIVER CHANGED. The only trip is P/E on FY2025 EPS, which is depressed by the Q2 2025 Day-1 Discover CECL loss (-$4,277m) and a part-year of Discover on the full post-deal share count. Priority-1 (normalise the earnings base) is already built into the model: it capitalises a normalised FY2026E FCFE with a through-cycle provision (24.7% of revenue vs 21.0% actually booked in 9M26). Priority-2 WACC premium rejected as double-counting the bear flows and 25% bear weight; priority-3 growth cap does not bind (3-5% path vs 8.7% organic CAGR); priority-4 EV/EBITDA cap not applicable to a bank. See valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_banner.

implied_multiples_after_fix.note: Unchanged because no driver was changed; the two extra P/E lines use hand-computed denominators (TTM ~$15.7, normalised FY26E ~$20.3) and are approximate.
